messages:
devon_arch: quick RFC follow-up: I pushed a narrower proposal for rollback safety in on‑prem / air‑gapped upgrades. main changes are a two-phase activation handshake, signed epoch manifests, and an operator eviction grace window. link: https://rfd/internal/airgap-rollback-safety v2

maya: skimmed it. can you summarize the failure-mode for powerloss mid-apply? we need a clear admin recovery path.

devon_arch: yep. short answer: we keep the previous image active until the new epoch reaches a 'commit' fence. the operator writes a signed activation intent, stages payloads to /var/lib/redwood/staged, verifies signatures, then performs a final atomic swap. if powerloss before commit -> operator resumes from staged and either retries apply or rolls back to previous activation depending on health probes.

sam: how does the signed activation intent prevent a partial-apply from being accepted by a different operator after reseed? attacker could inject a stale staged payload if keys rotate poorly.

devon_arch: good point. we tie activation intents to an epoch nonce bound to the manifest and to operator instance id + signed timestamp. rotation model: offline key escrow + KMS rewrap. if a reseed happens we require the operator to present the last known epoch checkpoint signed by the same key family or an administratively approved rekey token.

lee_sre: we should make the health probe conservative: only commit when app-level readiness is good for N consecutive checks. otherwise auto-abort and keep old activation. Also backoff retries to avoid fleet-wide flapping.

maya: +1 on consecutive checks. also request a manual override path: ops can force commit (for one-off emergency) but it must be logged and require 2 reviewers in audit log.

devon_arch: agree. I'll add a runbook step and API for force-commit that requires dual-approval. sample CLI for inspectors: 
```
# check activation status on node
redwood-operator inspect --node node-17 --activation-status
# possible states: PREPARED, INTENT-SIGNED, COMMITTED, ROLLED_BACK
```

sam: minor: include signature header fields in manifest: key-id, epoch-nonce, prev-checkpoint, and operator-id. that will make offline verification deterministic.

devon_arch: noted, will add JSON schema snippet. also adding a tiny TTL for staged artifacts so a stale stage expires after X days unless revalidated by an admin token. avoids disk bloat and attack surface.

lee_sre: what about operator eviction during apply? e.g., node OOM / kube evicted the operator pod mid-commit. we need an idempotent finalization so a second operator can detect partial swap and either resume commit or rollback.

devon_arch: design: finalization is idempotent and guarded by a commit lock in persistent store (etcd or on-disk lockfile for airgap). commit includes atomic rename of active -> active.old and staged -> active. if lock exists and manifest mismatch -> refuse until admin reconciles. that plus the signed intent prevents split-brain.

maya: pls add a short matrix of recovery scenarios in RFC (powerloss, pod-eviction, disk corruption, bad manifest). operators should have an explicit 'resume' verb and a 'repair' hook.

ops-bot: deploycheck: canary rollout simulation scheduled for staging cluster at 2026-04-02T03:00Z. targeting 10 nodes, abort on >1 unrecoverable resumption.

devon_arch: thanks @ops-bot. I'll update the RFC with the health-check thresholds, dual-approval flow, and the manifest JSON schema. ping me if you want to pair on the runbook. :+1:
